subject: Quantive Labs — Integration action matrix & JSON reliability plan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quantive Labs — Integration action matrix & JSON reliability plan

Thanks again for a focused call today — appreciate the clarity on the reranker use case and the latency targets. Short recap + proposed plan so we can lock next steps: 

Summary of discovery
- Goal: Integrate Redwood generation + reranker into Quantive's candidate scoring pipeline for doc summarization and triage.
- SLOs: 300 ms p95 for in-path scoring in the fastest flow; 1.2s for full rerank roundtrip.
- Data constraints: PII redaction required, VPC/private deployment preferred for production.

High-level integration items (proposed owners & ask)
1) SDK bootstrap and auth model (Rishi / Karthik) — action: choose between using our client SDK vs direct REST. We recommend using the SDK for token refresh + streaming ease, but both are supported. See attached "sdk-snippets.md".
2) Auth & keying (Quantive decision) — options: (A) Redwood short-lived bearer tokens issued via OIDC exchange with your IdP; (B) long-lived API key scoped to project (less preferred for production). We'll send the OIDC flow example.
3) Routing & failover (Karthik) — policy to prefer us-west for latency and fallback to secondary model variant when capacity constrained. We'll provide a routing-policy example.
4) Structured output reliability (Rishi / Monica) — JSON schema-first approach: 1) constrained decoding (schema-guided generation), 2) server-side validation, 3) deterministic repair + retry policy. See detailed pattern below.
5) Embeddings + reranker placement (Quantive + Rishi) — decision: client-side embedding vs server-side. We discussed tradeoffs; list below.

Structured output — proposed reliability pattern
- At generation time: use Redwood's structured output tooling to emit a JSON object that conforms to a supplied schema (attached schema-v1.json). Use field-level types and nominal enums where possible.
- Server-side validation: always validate the returned blob against the schema (JSON Schema draft-07). If valid -> proceed to reranker.
- If invalid: run a lightweight auto-correct pass ("canonicalizer") that handles common issues (trailing commas, unquoted keys, single->double quotes, missing closing brace). If canonicalizer succeeds -> re-validate.
- Retry policy after validation fail: automated policy = 2 retries maximum. Retry 1: deterministic retry with same prompt but stricter decoding params (temperature 0.0, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens conservative) and schema priming. Retry 2: model fallback to a verified-robust variant (e.g., redwood-structured-v1) with same strict params. If still invalid -> return structured error (400-ish) with the original output attached and a recommended remediation.
- Observability: log both raw model output and canonicalized output, validation result, and which fallback (if any) was used. TTL the raw logs per your retention policy.

Embeddings & reranker notes
- Option A (server-side embeddings): Redwood generates embeddings using a pinned model -> we store embeddings in your vector store (you can choose managed or self-hosted). Pros: model parity, easier governance; Cons: slightly higher server-side cost.
- Option B (client-side embeddings): Quantive generates embeddings locally and sends vectors to Redwood to score/rerank. Pros: data never leaves client; Cons: drift if embedding model/version mismatches. If you go client-side, include an "embed_version" metadata field and a checksum.

Next steps we agreed on during call
- I will share an action matrix and initial schema (attached). (Rishi) — by EOD tomorrow.
- Quantive to confirm embedding preference and whether they can run a short sandbox with client-side embedding. (Alex / Priya) — by next Tue 2028-04-03.
- Tech deep-dive session with Karthik + Monica to walk SDK snippets and auth flow. (Quantive + Redwood) — propose slot Wed 2028-04-04 10:00 PT.

Attachments: quantive-integration-action-matrix.xlsx, schema-v1.json, sdk-snippets.md

If that all looks right I’ll update the matrix with owners/dates and create a short PRD for the technical runbook.

Thanks,

1) Embeddings: Our security team prefers client-side embedding to reduce data movement. If we do client-side, can you confirm the minimum requirements for the embedding model (dimension, normalization) and exactly what metadata we must attach so Redwood can safely rerank?

2) Invalid JSON handling: you propose 2 retries. In the worst case that forces a user-visible fallback, what's the UX you recommend? Should we show a degraded summary or an error? Our concern is not surprising end users in the triage flow.

3) Latency: are the retry loops synchronous (visible to the user) or should we try a best-effort immediate sanitized fallback and kick off an async regeneration to surface later?

Alex — great questions, answers below and a recommended UX pattern.

1) Client-side embedding minimums we require
- Dimension: 1536 (default) or a pinned dimension you select (we support 512/1024/1536).
- Norm: L2-normalized vectors; include float32 array in standard JSON envelope.
- Metadata: include embed_version, model_id, document_id, and embedding_checksum (sha256 of the original text). Send as metadata alongside the vector. If you do client-side, we’ll validate the checksum and model_id on ingest and reject mismatches.

2) UX for invalid JSON / degraded flows
- Immediate UX: present a graceful degraded summary ("summary unavailable — generating condensed preview") rather than a hard error. The degraded summary should be generated from the raw model output using a short deterministic cleanup pipeline (we can provide a template).
- Async remediation: kick off an async regeneration with the strict decoding + model fallback and notify the user in-app/via websocket when the higher-fidelity result completes. This keeps critical flows smooth while improving quality behind the scenes.

3) Retry semantics and latency tradeoff
- Synchronous retries: keep very short (<= 300ms each) and only for quick validation failures that canonicalizer fixes. The deterministic retry with lower temperature tends to be fast when the model just produced a minor formatting error.
- Asynchronous retries: for cases requiring model fallback or longer decode runs, perform async regeneration so user latency isn't harmed. Surface the quick degraded result immediately and update when the robust pass finishes.

Implementation specifics (how we recommend you wire it)
- SDK: use Redwood SDK for streaming + builtin schema priming. See sdk-snippets.md for sample node/python snippets.
- Auth: prefer OIDC exchange with short-lived tokens for the production service account. We'll send an example assertion exchange flow and a Postman collection.
- Routing: include a request header x-quantive-region-preference. We'll map the header to our routing policy and provide an override for testing.
- Reranker flow: accept client-side vectors but require embed_version and checksum. If you want zero-data-leak, choose private deployment and server-side embedding with a pinned model.

Updated next steps / deadlines

- Alex/Priya to confirm embedding approach so we can provision test indexes (Quantive) — by 2028-04-03.
- Tech deep-dive Wed 2028-04-04 10:00 PT — confirmed calendar invite to follow. (Monica to schedule).

If that works I’ll publish the runbook PR and add a short set of acceptance tests (schema checks + latency smoke).
